stem: According to the line graph, between which two consecutive years did the number of enrolled learners decrease the most?
stimulus: A regional council runs a revitalization program for an endangered language. The line graph shows the number of learners enrolled in the program at the start of each year from 2016 to 2023.

figure.caption: Learners Enrolled in a Language Revitalization Program
figure.alt: Line graph of learners enrolled by year, 2016 to 2023, with the vertical axis running from 100 to 280 in steps of 20.

explanation: Work out the change for each choice: 2017 to 2018 is 200 to 180 (down 20), 2018 to 2019 is 180 to 260 (up 80), 2019 to 2020 is 260 to 220 (down 40), and 2021 to 2022 is 240 to 160 (down 80). The biggest decrease is 80 learners, from 2021 to 2022.

A.why: Enrollment does fall from 2017 to 2018, but only by 20. You stopped at the first decrease you saw and didn't compare it with the later drops of 40 and 80.

B.why: From 2018 to 2019 the line has its steepest rise, up 80. That's the biggest increase, and the question asks for a decrease.

C.why: The drop from 2019 to 2020 starts at the highest point on the graph, 260. Even so, enrollment falls only 40 there. You focused on the highest value instead of the size of the change.

stem: Based on the line graph, during which of the following periods did the median running time change by the greatest amount?
stimulus: A musicologist collected commercial recordings of one nineteenth-century symphony. For each decade's recordings, she found the median running time of a complete performance. The line graph shows the results.

figure.caption: Median Running Time of Recorded Performances of a Symphony
figure.alt: Line graph of median running time in minutes for recordings from 1950 to 2020, with the vertical axis running from 36 to 56 in steps of 2.

explanation: 'Change' counts movement in either direction, so compare the size of each change. 1950 to 1960 is up 6 minutes, 1970 to 1980 is down 2, 1990 to 2000 is down 14 (54 to 40), and 2000 to 2010 is up 10. The largest change is 14 minutes, from 1990 to 2000.

A.why: The period from 1950 to 1960 starts at the lowest point on the graph, 38 minutes. The running time changes by only 6 minutes there. You picked an extreme value instead of the largest change.

B.why: The running time does fall from 1970 to 1980, but only by 2 minutes. You found a change without checking that it was the greatest one.

D.why: The gain of 10 minutes from 2000 to 2010 is the largest increase. You read 'change' as 'increase' and missed the larger 14-minute decrease from 1990 to 2000.

stem: According to the line graph, between which two consecutive years did the number of bike-share trips increase the most?
stimulus: A city planning office tracks use of its public bike-share system. The line graph shows the total number of bike-share trips taken each year from 2015 to 2022.

figure.caption: Annual Bike-Share Trips in a City
figure.alt: Line graph of annual bike-share trips in thousands, 2015 to 2022, with the vertical axis running from 10 to 40 in steps of 2.

explanation: Find the change for each choice: 2015 to 2016 is up 8 thousand, 2017 to 2018 is up 12 thousand (22 to 34), 2019 to 2020 is down 8 thousand, and 2021 to 2022 is up 6 thousand. The largest increase is 12 thousand trips, from 2017 to 2018.

A.why: The period from 2015 to 2016 starts at the lowest point on the graph, but trips rise by only 8 thousand there, less than the 12 thousand from 2017 to 2018. You went by the starting value instead of the size of the rise.

C.why: From 2019 to 2020, trips fell by 8 thousand. That's a decrease, and the question asks for the greatest increase.

D.why: The period from 2021 to 2022 ends at the highest point on the graph, 38 thousand, but the rise is only 6 thousand. You compared where the segments end instead of how much each one climbs.

stem: Based on the line graph, in which year was the average number of sunspot groups per month first less than half the average for 2014?
stimulus: Volunteers at a small observatory count the sunspot groups visible on each clear day and record a monthly average. The line graph shows the average number of sunspot groups per month for each year from 2014 to 2021.

figure.caption: Average Sunspot Groups Recorded per Month
figure.alt: Line graph of average sunspot groups per month, 2014 to 2021, with the vertical axis running from 0 to 65 in steps of 5.

explanation: The 2014 average is 60 groups, so half of it is 30. The value has to be less than 30. It is exactly 30 in 2017, and it first drops below 30 in 2018, at 20 groups.

A.why: In 2017 the average is exactly 30, which equals half the 2014 value but isn't less than it. You ignored the strict 'less than.'

C.why: 2019 is the lowest point on the graph, at 10 groups. That's below 30, but it isn't the first year below 30. You answered 'lowest' instead of the condition the question gives.

D.why: The 2021 average of 25 is below 30, but it's the last year below half, not the first. You read the graph from the wrong end.

stem: Of the following 2-year periods, during which did average daily crossings on the bridge increase the most?
stimulus: Civil engineers monitoring a river bridge record its average daily vehicle crossings each year to plan maintenance. The line graph shows these averages from 2012 to 2020.

figure.caption: Average Daily Vehicle Crossings on a River Bridge
figure.alt: Line graph of average daily vehicle crossings in thousands, 2012 to 2020, with the vertical axis running from 28 to 50 in steps of 2.

explanation: For each 2-year period, compare the value at the start with the value at the end. 2016 to 2018 is 36 to 46 (up 10 thousand), 2014 to 2016 is 34 to 36 (up 2 thousand), 2015 to 2017 is 48 to 40 (down 8 thousand), and 2017 to 2019 is 40 to 48 (up 8 thousand). The largest increase is 10 thousand, from 2016 to 2018.

B.why: The steepest single segment on the graph, 2014 to 2015, falls inside this period. Crossings drop again by 2016, though, so the net gain over the 2 years is only 2 thousand. You stopped after the first year instead of measuring the whole period.

C.why: From 2015 to 2017, crossings fell from 48 to 40 thousand. That's a decrease, and the question asks for an increase.

D.why: This period ends at 48 thousand, the highest endpoint among the choices, but the rise is only 8 thousand. You compared ending values instead of the change across each period.
